kai: proposing a small experiment and a config for a waveform-based synthetic generator to better probe long-tail behavior while exercising kernel selection and KV warmup knobs. TL;DR: smooth ramp + controlled microbursts + prefix-warmup phases so kernels/memory layouts settle before heavy tail.
sana: sounds useful. can you paste the config and the metrics you want to record?

omar: also want to know how this differs from the current poisson + step ramp we use. trying to avoid duplicate runs.

kai: summary first: goals: 1) produce reproducible long-tail tails for apples-to-apples compare across kernels, 2) expose KV cold->hot transitions (so we can validate cache eviction heuristics), 3) create bursts narrow enough to stress batching heuristics without saturating GPU memory.

config snippet (json):
```json
{
  "waveform": "sine",
  "base_qps": 5,
  "amplitude_qps": 180,
  "period_s": 600,
  "microburst": {
    "enabled": true,
    "freq_per_min": 6,
    "burst_qps": 1200,
    "burst_duration_ms": 350
  },
  "kv_warmup": {
    "prefix_ratio": 0.25,
    "stagger_secs": 15
  },
  "seed": 1729,
  "request_profile": "client-latency-track.json"
}
```

kai: metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99/p999 latency, token throughput, per-request batch size distribution, kernel version tag, GPU mem alloc high-water, KV hit/miss by shard, tail-replay traces (sampled 1/1000).

juhi: for KV warmup: prefix_ratio means fraction of requests that include cached prefix? and stagger_secs is offset between client shards?

kai: exactly. prefix_ratio 0.25 means 25% of requests include a hot prefix that should populate the KV cache. stagger_secs staggers the warmup windows across worker groups so cache fills more naturally instead of all at once.

omar: how do we encode kernel selection in the harness? want to make sure the runtime isn't auto-fallbacking mid-run because of perf-telemetry.

kai: harness will pin kernel via env var INFER_KERNEL_OVERRIDE and also record the runtime-decided kernel tag. we'll disable automated fallback for the run (config flag) to keep experiments apples-to-apples. fallback still available in prod but not for these measurements.

loadgen-bot: run queued: id=rg-waveform-2024-11-03-01, started at 1745003001, pinned_kernel=fast-attn-v3, fallback_disabled=true

omi: (typo: omi is not listed)

juhi: quick perf-reg checklist: 1) seed RNG recorded 2) workload artifacts uploaded (prometheus + jaeger + sample-requests) 3) env + docker image tag saved 4) KV shard map version captured.

kai: yes to all. I'm attaching a small tracer snippet for batch-size histogram collection:
```python
# in runner
batch_hist.observe(len(requests))
for r in requests:
  span.annotate("kernel", os.getenv("INFER_KERNEL_TAG"))
```

omar: run results posted: p50=18ms p95=72ms p99=180ms p999=420ms, median batch size=3, p95 batch size=7. KV hit-rate during ramp: 18% -> 83% over first 4 minutes. GPU mem peaks at 12.3GB on bursts.

kai: nice. any weird regressions vs baseline (fast-attn-v2 baseline run from last week)?

omar: compared to v2 baseline: p99 up ~12% on microburst edges, p999 up ~9%. Kernel v3 improved avg latency by ~6% but had slightly larger variance under high burst QPS. suspect kernel scheduling jitter + packing threshold.

juhi: can we correlate batch packing threshold events with KV misses? maybe cache miss causes longer generation and reduces packing, leading to smaller batches and higher tail.

kai: good idea. if we overlay per-request KV hit flag with batch size timeline we can test that hypothesis. add a label kv_hit:true/false to sampled traces.

omar: adding that now and re-running the 2-hour sweep next window. also toggling microburst.duration to 650ms to see if slightly longer bursts smooth the p999.

kai: next steps: 1) run v2/v3 side-by-side with identical seeds + kv shard map, 2) collect per-batch kernel tag and batch-size correlation, 3) add an experiment that forces cold-KV by zeroing prefix cache between microbursts.

sana: logging these in the perf board. thanks, team. :thumbsup:
